body.x: Conventional printed circuit boards (PCBs) and flexible PCBs (FPCBs) can bend, but they have limits when a device must follow the curves and movement of the human body, or the joints of a robot.
What if the circuit itself could stretch?

T&L Healthcare, founded in 2023 and led by CEO Dogi Pyeon, builds its business on a patented technology called SPCB, or Stretchable PCB. At KES 2026, the company is focusing on technology and module sales and is showing SPCB-based products, including COMLAX, NECKCARE BAND GOLDEN and the LED Cool Face Mask.

SPCB combines high flexibility with stretchability, and the company says it can be integrated with LEDs, sensors and other functions. That allows T&L Healthcare to develop customized modules and devices for wearables, body-conforming patches, robotics and other products that need flexible, dynamic structures, and to work with partners on OEM and ODM projects.

Since 2025, the company has signed memorandums of understanding with major Korean corporations and with healthcare and beauty companies. It is running joint R&D projects with partners that want to apply SPCB to new products, including wearable devices, patches and LED-based solutions, and is also pursuing B2B collaboration through technology and module supply and custom product development.

T&L Healthcare has no export sales yet. Rather than targeting specific countries, it plans to enter markets where demand for SPCB is strong, and it is looking for partners that develop or manufacture wearables, patches, healthcare and beauty devices, robotics and other products requiring flexibility and stretchability. Its aims at KES are to find new partners for technology application and joint R&D and to widen opportunities for commercialization. The company says identifying overseas buyers and understanding local market demand are its main challenges, and that help finding technology-demanding companies and local market information would speed up its entry.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
